nonLabourLines.description: Data migration tooling / Oracle export licensing

assumptions: No historical actuals (real spend data) are available yet for this project; estimate is based on story points, task descriptions, and standard delivery ratios only.
Story points roughly map to effort at ~8-10 hours/point for backend-heavy work, adjusted per task complexity (e.g. migration and RBAC skew higher due to risk/complexity, not just points).

Backend Developer capacity (1.5 FTE) is the primary bottleneck given the backlog's backend-heavy nature (auth, RBAC, payments, migration); 520 hours assumes ~3.3 months at 1.5 FTE (about 693 hrs available), leaving some buffer but this role is staffed thinly relative to demand.
Frontend Developer (1.0 FTE) hours cover design system, dashboard, invoice UI, and RBAC UI work.

QA Engineer (0.6 FTE) hours are allocated across all features but are not exhaustive full-regression coverage per story; assumes risk-based testing focused on Urgent/High priority items (auth, RBAC, payments).

DevOps Engineer (0.4 FTE) hours cover CI/staging setup (PW-1) plus ongoing pipeline support and Stripe webhook infra hardening; this is a thin allocation and DevOps could become a bottleneck if issues arise during payment integration or migration cutover.

Legacy data migration (PW-8) is assumed to require significant Backend Developer time for ETL scripting plus non-labour tooling cost; actual record complexity/data quality is unknown and could shift this significantly.

Payment provider integration (PW-7) assumes standard Stripe Checkout/Payment Intents flow with webhooks; deep reconciliation logic against legacy invoicing could add hours if requirements are more complex than assumed.
Non-labour costs are rough placeholders for tooling/licensing/sandbox fees; actual figures depend on vendor contracts not provided.
Scenario spread (Optimistic -12.7%, Pessimistic +17.6%) reflects uncertainty from thin DevOps/QA staffing and undefined legacy data quality, rather than precise probabilistic modelling.
input.reasoning: Effort was estimated per backlog item using story points as a rough proxy for complexity, then allocated across the four staffed roles based on the nature of each task (e.g., PW-8 migration is backend+non-labour heavy; PW-2 design system is frontend-heavy; PW-3/PW-4/PW-7 require balanced backend/frontend/QA work given their security and compliance sensitivity). Backend Developer received the largest hour allocation reflecting the backend-heavy nature of auth, RBAC, payments and migration work, and because it has the largest FTE pool (1.5) to draw from. QA and DevOps hours were kept proportionate to their smaller FTE allocations (0.6 and 0.4 respectively), focused on the highest-risk/priority items rather than uniform coverage across all 8 tasks — this is flagged as a staffing thinness risk in the assumptions. Non-labour costs cover expected third-party/tooling costs for Stripe integration and Oracle data migration tooling, plus minor staging infrastructure setup cost. The three scenarios (Optimistic/Most Likely/Pessimistic) were built around the reconciled line-item total of $108,831.60, with a -12.7%/+17.6% spread reflecting the biggest uncertainty drivers: legacy data quality/volume for PW-8 and the thin DevOps/QA staffing that could cause delays if issues surface during payment or migration cutover.

reductions.description: Descope PW-2 (Design system and component library) to a minimal set (buttons, forms, tables only) and defer full theming tokens/dialogs to a later phase, since it's Medium priority and not blocking core urgent features.
reductions.effect: Reduces Frontend Developer hours by ~65 hours; theming and dialog components deferred to a post-launch iteration.

reductions.description: Defer PW-6 (Invoice list and detail view) PDF download feature to a fast-follow release, shipping only the list/filter/detail view initially.
reductions.effect: Reduces Backend and Frontend hours associated with PDF generation/rendering by roughly 45 combined hours.

reductions.description: Reduce QA scope on Medium-priority items (PW-2, PW-6) to smoke testing only, focusing full QA effort on Urgent/High priority items (auth, RBAC, payments, migration).
reductions.effect: Cuts QA Engineer hours by ~30 hours; residual regression risk on lower-priority UI features is accepted.

reductions.description: Phase PW-8 (Legacy data migration) into two stages: migrate customer records now, defer the 2M invoice line migration to a subsequent phase once the pipeline is validated at smaller scale.
reductions.effect: Reduces Backend Developer hours on migration scripting/testing by ~90 hours and defers associated tooling/licensing non-labour spend of ~$750 to a later budget cycle.

reductions.description: Use Stripe's hosted Checkout page instead of a fully custom payment UI/flow for PW-7, reducing custom frontend and backend integration work while still meeting the Urgent priority requirement.
reductions.effect: Reduces combined Backend and Frontend hours on payment UI/flow by ~35 hours; reconciliation logic still fully implemented.
